The '''Invasion of Batravalka''' was a 1971 territorial crisis under the Istragarde treaty system.

== Background ==

The Istragarde source says [[Karlist Perzam]] invoked the [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]] to justify a surprise invasion of the mineral-rich Batravalka highlands. Perzam framed the campaign around historical claims and the protection of ethnic Perzamic communities.

== International Response ==

International condemnation followed, but no military response was organized. The [[Istragarde Tribunal]] and treaty framework lacked the direct enforcement mechanisms needed to reverse the invasion by force.

== Legacy ==

The invasion became an early example of the Istragarde system's weakness. Later states, especially the [[Volgastan Baathist Republic]] through the [[Volgastani Expansionist Doctrine]], used similar treaty ambiguity and cultural-protection language to defend expansion.
